architecture_observed.pipeline: eBPF programs -> JSON stdout -> capture core -> analysis extension -> output/web/files
capture_mechanisms: SSL_read/SSL_write uprobes for TLS plaintext where attachable
architecture_observed.platform_boundary: Portable top/bind/vis/report paths work without eBPF across major desktop OSes; eBPF record/debug capture is Linux-specific and privilege-sensitive.
architecture_observed.timestamp_boundary: Kernel events use nanoseconds since boot and are converted to wall time using boot time; direct F2 causal identity is not inherent.

privilege_and_security_boundary: eBPF capture requires sudo or CAP_BPF plus CAP_SYS_ADMIN according to upstream guidance
privileged Docker/host PID access may be required for container observation
captured session databases can contain prompts, responses, file paths, headers and network targets and must be treated as sensitive
TLS plaintext interception is an observability mechanism, not an authority mechanism
known_visibility_gaps: Electron IDE agents are not generally observable via the eBPF TLS path and use agent-native session fallbacks
statically linked SSL/BoringSSL/OpenSSL agents require binary discovery/attachment handling
protobuf/non-JSON traffic may produce no LLM event even when transport capture succeeds

hypothesis: A source-pinned, read-only AgentSight-derived witness can expose subprocess/file/network/resource evidence that F2 application telemetry may miss, improving failure diagnosis and telemetry ablations without becoming canonical state or effect authority.
counterhypotheses: F2-native telemetry can cover the same discriminators with less privilege and dependency weight.
eBPF/TLS capture gaps and vendor-specific session fallbacks can create misleading partial visibility.
Importing AgentSight storage or analysis as mutable operational state could create a second truth store and violate UnifiedDB authority.
Boot-relative timestamps and independently inferred sessions may not bind cleanly to F2 causal_event_id/tool_use_id/effect_id without an explicit adapter.
TLS plaintext capture creates privacy and secret-handling risk that outweighs diagnostic value in routine operation.
The full upstream stack is heavier than the useful mechanism; a thin structural distillation may dominate direct adoption.

allowed: read exported AgentSight SQLite/OTel/event artifacts as noncanonical evidence
bind imported witness rows to exact F2 run_id/process identity/time window/source pin
store only typed witness references/digests and reconciled observations in canonical F2 evidence tables
use witness disagreement as a trigger for investigation
forbidden: AgentSight database as canonical F2 truth
silent capture of secrets or TLS payloads in normal production mode
architecture promotion from README/upstream benchmark claims
